title: Accelerating Aggregation Queries on Unstructured Streams of Data
note: Approximate aggregation over streams processed by expensive ML models, with a sampling/scheduling policy; one GPU is enough

title: The RLR-Tree: A Reinforcement Learning Based R-Tree for Spatial Data
note: Reinforcement learning drives R-tree ChooseSubtree and Split without changing the index structure - a learned policy inside a system, CPU only

title: QPET: A Versatile and Portable Quantity-of-Interest-preservation Framework for Error-Bounded Lossy Compression
note: Error-bounded lossy compression framework layered on existing compressors; user-space C++ on one node

title: TensorIR: An Abstraction for Automatic Tensorized Program Optimization
note: Tensorized-program abstraction for TVM - single GPU/CPU auto-scheduling  fully open source and upstreamed into Apache TVM

title: Orthrus: Efficient and Timely Detection of Silent User Data Corruption in the Cloud with Resource-Adaptive Computation Validation
note: User-space runtime plus an LLVM compiler pass that re-validates annotated data operators asynchronously on spare cores; the whole experiment (including LLVM-based fault injection, see the companion Orthrus-FaultInjection repo) is single-machine and root-free. Concerns - the README states a minimum of 48 cores for the test scripts and this machine has 16 cores / 32 threads, so the core-scaling experiments must be rescaled and the 4-validation-core points re-interpreted.

title: Supporting Descendants in SIMD-Accelerated JSONPath
note: SIMD JSONPath query engine in Rust with descendant support - CPU only user space  actively maintained open source with a benchmark harness

title: Disco: A Compact Index for LSM-trees
note: Compact index for LSM-trees, integrated in a key-value store; user space

title: MIRAGE-ANNS: Mixed Approach Graph-based Indexing for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Graph-based ANN index combining clustering and graph traversal; single machine

title: Graph Neural Network Training Systems: A Performance Comparison of Full-Graph and Mini-Batch.
note: Time-to-accuracy comparison of full-graph vs mini-batch GNN training systems. Concern: several baselines are multi-GPU or multi-node so a single-GPU subset must be chosen

title: Explore Data Placement Algorithm for Balanced Recovery Load Distribution
note: The contribution is an NP-hardness formulation plus a greedy data-placement algorithm - an algorithmic storage-placement result that can be evaluated by simulation/microbenchmark on one machine. Two artifacts released: rcstor/greedy_microbenchmark (the placement microbenchmark) and rcstor/rcstor (the full system); AE Available+Functional. Concerns: the end-to-end recovery-speed numbers came from a real multi-disk cluster, so only the simulated/microbenchmark half is reproducible here.

title: LoRAFusion: Efficient LoRA Fine-Tuning for LLMs
note: LoRA fine-tuning kernel fusion and multi-adapter batching - the fusion part is a single-GPU kernel contribution. Concern: paper also targets multi-GPU pipelines that will not fit

title: AgentTune: An Agent-Based Large Language Model Framework for Database Knob Tuning
note: agent/LLM-based DBMS knob tuning - ML-based tuning of a system - runs against a local PostgreSQL/MySQL - concern: needs an LLM endpoint and no repo located

title: Heron: Automatically Constrained High-Performance Library Generation for Deep Learning Accelerators
note: Constrained auto-scheduling for tensor libraries - supports NVIDIA tensor-core GPUs and CPUs; concern part of the evaluation uses a Cambricon accelerator we do not have

title: FileScale: Fast and Elastic Metadata Management for Distributed File Systems
note: Three-tier HDFS metadata architecture (in-memory tier plus distributed DBMS tier); all Java/user space, no root needed, and the paper's distinguishing claim - matching single-machine in-memory performance at small scale - is exactly the regime this host can test. Concern: the linear-scalability half of the evaluation needs several nodes; it can only be approximated with multiple JVMs on the 16-core host, and Java must be installed per-user.

title: Robust Recursive Query Parallelism in Graph Database Management Systems
note: Morsel dispatching policies for parallel recursive joins in Kuzu - a multicore task-scheduling design space study; artifact is a Kuzu fork

title: Slapo: A Schedule Language for Progressive Optimization of Large Deep Learning Model Training
note: Schedule language decoupling PyTorch model definition from optimization. Concern - 3D-parallelism results need many GPUs; single-GPU primitives (kernel replacement, activation checkpointing) are still evaluable. Artifact repo is chhzh123/slapo-artifact.

title: SecretFlow-SPU: A Performant and User-Friendly Framework for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
note: Frontend compiler plus backend runtime that lowers ordinary JAX/TF ML programs to an MPC IR - a user-space ML compiler/runtime, exactly the ml-systems bucket. All parties can be run as separate processes on one host and the artifact is AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the contribution is heavily cryptographic rather than architectural; the WAN results use link emulation (tc/netem) which needs root, so only LAN/localhost numbers are reproducible here.

title: RTIndeX: Exploiting Hardware-Accelerated GPU Raytracing for Database Indexing
note: Maps database point/range indexing onto NVIDIA OptiX raytracing cores; a pure user-space CUDA/OptiX artifact, no root, no kernel, no cluster. The machine fit is unusually good: the paper's Section 4.10 explicitly re-runs the study on Ampere and Turing RTX GPUs besides the RTX 4090, and our RTX A5000 is Ampere with RT cores and exactly 24 GB VRAM (same capacity as their main 4090 system), so datasets sized in the paper fit. Carries the PVLDB "Results Reproduced" badge. Concerns: (a) the artifact is on GitLab (gitlab.rlp.net), reachable and live, not GitHub; (b) the authors use Nsight Systems/Nsight Compute for some breakdowns - GPU profiling may be blocked by the driver's admin-only profiling setting, so a project should plan on wall-clock timing only; (c) OptiX SDK must be installed per-user, and CUDA 11.8/driver 535 support OptiX 7.x. [PVLDB 16(13), added from the vldbgap-2024 shard]

title: Caravan: Practical Online Learning of In-Network ML Models with Labeling Agents
note: Online retraining and labeling pipeline for learned network models. Artifact appendix asks for an 8-core server 16 GiB RAM and one CUDA 12.1 GPU which this machine exceeds. Concern - the optional in-network deployment uses an FPGA testbed and must be skipped

title: Nixie: Efficient, Transparent Temporal Multiplexing for Consumer GPUs
note: Best-matched paper in the venue for this machine: a *user-space system service* that time-multiplexes several near-GPU-memory-filling ML jobs on a **consumer GPU** with "no application or driver changes", plus an MLFQ-style scheduler. Eval repo: https://github.com/XOR-op/nixie-eval . Concern: pinned-host-memory pressure experiments assume a large host RAM budget (we have it)

title: 3L-Cache: Low Overhead and Precise Learning-based Eviction Policy for Caches
note: Learning-based cache eviction policy evaluated entirely by trace-driven simulation on top of libCacheSim - user-space C++, CPU only, no root, and the headline metric (CPU overhead vs miss ratio) is exactly the kind of trade-off a 10-week improvement project can attack. Concerns - the paper's 4855-trace corpus is many TB; must subset to a few trace families and argue representativeness.

title: Using Lock-Free Design for Throughput-Optimized Cache Eviction (Mobius)
note: Lock-free FIFO-queue cache eviction policy (SIEVE-like) evaluated for concurrent throughput and hit ratio; pure user-space C++ integrated into CacheLib and RocksDB. Ideal fit for a 16-core/32-thread box. Second official repo is RocksDB-with-Mobius under the same account. Concern: the artifact account is an anonymized handle with no README-level build docs visible; scaling claims were made on a higher-core-count cluster so absolute numbers will differ.

title: Similarity search in the blink of an eye with compressed indices
note: Graph vector index with compressed vectors and SIMD kernels; single node, datasets fit in 125 GiB RAM. Concern: heavily tuned for Intel AVX-512, our Zen3 has AVX2 so absolute numbers will differ

title: GIANTSAN: Efficient Memory Sanitization with Segment Folding
note: LLVM-based memory sanitizer with a new shadow encoding; purely user-space, CPU-only. Concern - headline numbers use SPEC CPU2017 which is licensed; open benchmarks would have to substitute.

title: CausalMesh: A Causal Cache for Stateful Serverless Computing
note: causally consistent cache for stateful serverless workflows; the multi-server topology can be emulated with several processes on one host

title: RIB: Robust Learning-based Index Benefit Estimation
note: robust learned index-benefit estimator that tolerates noisy telemetry labels - learned system component - concern: built around a commercial tuner, code likely internal

title: Revisiting B-tree Compression: An Experimental Study
note: Experimental study of seven B-tree compression techniques - a reusable single-node index benchmark. Concern: checked GitHub repo search and web search, no artifact link found

title: Query Compilation Without Regrets
note: Trace-based JIT compiler framework for query engines - a user-space runtime/compiler artifact; CPU only

title: Accelerating Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning With GeniBatch
note: A user-space compiler that rewrites PHE-based ML programs into batched (SIMD-packed) ciphertext programs; built on FATE, all CPU. Concern - cross-silo setting means two or more parties, but they can be run as separate processes on one host; the speedup claims are compute-bound, the traffic claims are not reproducible without a real link

title: Oneiros: KV Cache Optimization through Parameter Remapping for Multi-tenant LLM Serving
note: Remaps memory holding model parameters into KV cache instead of swapping; pure user-space change on top of vLLM. A 7-8B FP16 model plus KV cache fits the 24 GB A5000. Concern - the multi-tenant results assume several resident models, so the study must be scaled down to small models or quantized ones. Also check that the CUDA 12.x wheels it needs run on driver 535.

title: Starling: An I/O-Efficient Disk-Resident Graph Index Framework for High-Dimensional Vector Similarity Search on Data Segment
note: I/O-efficient disk-resident graph index for vector search; explicitly designed for a small memory budget on a single node

title: ServerlessLLM: Low-Latency Serverless Inference for Large Language Models
note: Core contribution is a fast multi-tier checkpoint loading format plus locality-aware serverless scheduling - checkpoint loading from local NVMe to one GPU is directly reproducible. Concern - the scheduler and live migration parts assume a multi-GPU cluster and would have to be studied with a simulator or multiple processes

title: AQD: Online Adaptive Query Dispatcher for HTAP Databases
note: Learned online query dispatcher that routes queries between row and column engines with low latency. Concern: needs an HTAP dual-engine deployment

title: SPALM: A Sparsity-Pattern-Adaptive Library for Matrices
note: sparsity-pattern-adaptive matrix multiplication library integrated as a DuckDB operator - a CPU user-space numerical/systems library - concern: no repo located

title: Frequency Domain Data Encoding in Apache IoTDB
note: Frequency-domain lossy encoding for time-series storage; pure Java single node. Concern: artifact is a personal Apache IoTDB fork branch not upstream. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/543202718/iotdb/tree/research/descend .

title: NanoFlow: Towards Optimal Large Language Model Serving Throughput
note: Intra-device (single-GPU) operation overlap for LLM serving - the mechanism is explicitly *within* one device, so it scales down cleanly. Available + Functional + Reproduced; very active repo. Concerns: published numbers use 8xA100-80GB with LLaMA-2-70B; on one 24 GB A5000 the study must drop to 8B-class models, and the hand-tuned CUTLASS/FlashInfer kernels were built for sm_80/sm_90 so sm_86 re-tuning is likely needed.

title: Déjà Vu: Efficient Video-Language Query Engine with Learning-based Inter-Frame Computation Reuse
note: Inter-frame computation reuse for ViT-based video-language inference plus memory-compute compaction to turn FLOP savings into speedup; single GPU

title: SpareLLM: Automatically Selecting Task-Specific Minimum-Cost Large Language Models under Equivalence Constraint
note: Cost-aware selection/routing among LLMs under an equivalence constraint; concern - mainly uses hosted model APIs

title: GraCE: Unlocking CUDA Graphs with Compiler Support for ML Workloads
note: CPU-launch-overhead elimination for short ML kernels via CUDA Graphs - single GPU, TorchBench/HuggingFace/TIMM workloads, and launch overhead is *more* visible on a modest GPU. Concerns: the prebuilt artifact is a Docker image built for CUDA 12.8 (no Docker here, and driver 535 supports CUDA 12.2 natively) - needs a source build in a conda env

title: Serving Hybrid LLM Loads with SLO Guarantees Using CPU-GPU Attention Piggybacking
note: LLM serving system that offloads best-effort attention to CPUs to protect latency-sensitive SLOs - CPU-GPU co-scheduling for inference - concern: motivated by shared clusters - single-GPU co-location still reproducible - no repo located

title: Bullet: Boosting GPU Utilization for LLM Serving via Dynamic Spatial-Temporal Orchestration
note: Single-GPU spatial-temporal sharing of prefill and decode - exactly the kind of intra-GPU serving mechanism one A5000 can host with a 7B model

title: Out-of-Order Sliding-Window Aggregation with Efficient Bulk Evictions and Insertions
note: Out-of-order sliding-window aggregation data structures with bulk eviction/insertion; C++/Rust library, CPU-only microbenchmarks

title: UniTG: A Unified System for Efficient and Seamless Textual Graph Learning
note: Fuses the language model and GNN phases of textual graph learning into one runtime with co-designed components. Concern: larger language-model backbones may exceed 24 GB so a scaled-down backbone is needed

title: Ladder: Enabling Efficient Low-Precision Deep Learning Computing through Hardware-aware Tensor Transformation
note: Low-precision tensor compiler generating custom dtype kernels - evaluated on A100 V100 and RTX A6000 so the Ampere A5000 is a supported class of device. Concern - some dtype paths target newer toolkits and FP8 needs Ada/Hopper so those configurations must be dropped. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/BitBLAS/tree/osdi24_ladder_artifact .

title: Cocoon: A System Architecture for Differentially Private Training with Correlated Noises
note: Single-node DP-training framework; the artifact appendix says main experiments ran on **RTX A5000 24 GB** GPUs - the same GPU as this machine. Concern: their box has 4 A5000s and two sockets, so runs must be scaled to one GPU; some results are embedding-table-heavy

title: Hydro: Surrogate-Based Hyperparameter Tuning Service in Datacenters
note: Surrogate model scaling plus job fusion for hyperparameter tuning, built on Ray Tune; the Tuner half (model scaling, parametrization, fusion) is meaningful on a single GPU. Concern: the Coordinator half assumes a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster with ephemeral resources and would have to be simulated or dropped.

title: Tabular: Efficiently Building Efficient Indexes
note: Library that builds concurrent persistent indexes on top of an ACID table engine; user-space multicore system

title: TileClipper: Lightweight Selection of Regions of Interest from Videos for Traffic Surveillance
note: Video-analytics pipeline that selects tiles by bitrate before sending frames to a detector; artifact is user-space Python plus Kvazaar and YOLOv5 and runs on one GPU, with a clear bandwidth-versus-accuracy tradeoff to improve. Concern: the live-deployment numbers used Raspberry Pi and Jetson Nano edge devices that we do not have

title: LeCo: Lightweight Compression via Learning Serial Correlations
note: Learned lightweight column compression exploiting serial correlation; CPU only

title: Towards Affordable Reproducibility Using Scalable Capture and Comparison of Intermediate Multi-Run Results
note: Hash/Merkle-tree comparison of checkpoint data with error bounds; the artifact is a user-space C++/Kokkos library whose README cites this paper by DOI. The hashing, tree construction and I/O-reduction mechanisms are all measurable on one node. Concern: the paper drives the system from HACC cosmology runs on an HPC cluster, so a single-machine study needs scaled-down or synthetic checkpoint streams; build needs Kokkos, io_uring and optionally ADIOS2, all installable in $HOME.

title: LPLM: A Neural Language Model for Cardinality Estimation of LIKE-Queries
note: Neural language model for LIKE-query cardinality estimation; small models, single GPU

title: Keep It Simple: Testing Databases via Differential Query Plans
note: Differential-query-plan DBMS testing implemented in SQLancer; runs DBMSs in user space, no root

title: Characterizing Distributed Machine Learning Workloads on Apache Spark (Experimentation and Deployment Paper)
note: Studies the interplay of Spark platform parameters vs. ML hyper-parameters over 13 learning methods and 6 datasets; the headline claim (platform parameters matter more than hyper-parameters for model quality) is a clean testable hypothesis and Spark MLlib is pure user-space JVM code that runs in local/standalone mode on 16 cores and 125 GiB RAM. Concerns - the paper is a characterization study run on two multi-node clusters so absolute numbers will not reproduce on one node; the released artifact is mostly workload scripts plus traces rather than a system to improve; an improvement angle would have to be an auto-tuner built on their traces. Traces are also archived separately (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14151075)

title: Dalton: Learned Partitioning for Distributed Data Streams
note: RL-learned partitioning for stream operators. Concern: built on Apache Flink - the distributed setup must be emulated with local task managers on the 32 threads

title: Hotline Profiler: Automatic Annotation and A Multi-Scale Timeline for Visualizing Time-Use in DNN Training
note: Profiler that annotates standard PyTorch or Chrome trace data with DNN training-loop and model structure - explicitly avoids vendor-specific tools so it needs no perf counters and no root - concern - visualization front end plus a Zenodo artifact so check the trace collector still works with current PyTorch

title: Locality-Aware Cache Replacement Policy for Graph Traversals
note: LAC cache replacement policy evaluated both in a simulator and inside Neo4j - textbook eviction-policy work that a course project can extend

title: LMTracer: Fine-Grained and Real-Time Performance Profiling for Production LLM Systems
note: Fine-grained real-time profiler for LLM serving systems. Profiling and tracing work is user space. Serious concern: GPU-side fine-grained profiling usually needs CUPTI, and on driver 535 CUPTI profiling counters are admin-restricted by default - plus perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks CPU counters here. No preprint or artifact found.

title: Fractal: Fault-Tolerant Shell-Script Distribution
note: Fault-tolerant distributed shell-script execution with subgraph-level dependency and progress tracking - MIT-licensed, user-space, and the runtime can be driven with multiple worker processes on one host. Concern - the paper's speedups are measured on 4- and 30-node clusters so absolute numbers will not reproduce; fault-recovery semantics still can.

title: Gigaflow: Pipeline-Aware Sub-Traversal Caching for Modern SmartNICs
note: Pipeline-aware sub-traversal flow-cache design for vSwitches - the caching algorithm and its trace-driven evaluation are software; concern: the headline deployment is on a SmartNIC, so only the software vSwitch/simulation path is reproducible here

title: Phantora: Maximizing Code Reuse in Simulation-based Machine Learning System Performance Estimation
note: Hybrid GPU-cluster simulator that runs unmodified ML frameworks and intercepts GPU/comm calls, explicitly designed so cluster performance can be estimated from a single GPU. Concern - it emulates each GPU server as a container and Docker/Podman are not installed, so the container layer must be ported to bwrap or plain processes.

title: Event Tensor: A Unified Abstraction for Compiling Dynamic Megakernel
note: Compiler abstraction for dynamic megakernels that removes launch overhead in LLM inference; the mechanism is single-GPU persistent-kernel scheduling and fits the A5000 well. Concerns: the paper only states ETC was 'incorporated into a major open-source system' without naming a repository, so the code location is unknown

title: WACO: Learning Workload-Aware Co-optimization of the Format and Schedule of a Sparse Tensor Program
note: Learned cost model that co-optimizes sparse tensor format and schedule - CPU only  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: Avoiding the Ordering Trap in Systems Performance Measurement
note: Not a pure measurement study: OrderSage is a released, reusable user-space Python tool that randomizes trial order and runs statistical order-dependence tests, which is directly usable (and improvable) on this machine. Paper artifact at https://github.com/ordersage/paper-artifact. Concerns: the headline empirical result (2.3M measurements over 1,700 CloudLab servers) is not reproducible on one host - an improvement would have to target the tool's statistics/methodology, and validating it on a single shared machine introduces its own noise.

title: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications with Ayo
note: Primitive-level dataflow orchestration of LLM applications (RAG etc.) - user-space orchestration layer over a single-GPU engine

title: ShapleyIQ: Influence Quantification by Shapley Values for Performance Debugging of Microservices
note: Shapley-value performance attribution for microservice traces - code and data released; analysis runs offline on traces on one host  concern the original setting is a production cluster

title: QoServe: Breaking the Silos of LLM Inference Serving
note: QoS-driven scheduling on top of Sarathi-Serve; artifact is the niyama_asplos2026 branch. Concern: paper evaluates an A100 cluster so a single-replica scale-down is needed

title: ACORN: Performant and Predicate-Agnostic Search Over Vector Embeddings and Structured Data
note: Predicate-agnostic hybrid vector search built on FAISS/HNSW; CPU only, single node

title: EVT: Accelerating Deep Learning Training with Epilogue Visitor Tree
note: Epilogue Visitor Tree compiler for training-graph fusion built on CUTLASS; single GPU. Concern - CUTLASS templates were tuned for A100 (SM80); SM86 retuning may be needed.

title: CausalSim: A Causal Framework for Unbiased Trace-Driven Simulation
note: Causal correction for trace-driven simulation with released code and public Puffer RCT data - fully CPU and single-GPU friendly and a Best Paper - Concern: it is closer to a data-science pipeline than a running system so an improvement hypothesis must target the tensor-completion method or the ABR simulator and the trace download is large

title: SEFRQO: A Self-Evolving Fine-Tuned RAG-Based Query Optimizer
note: self-evolving RAG-based LLM query optimizer - learned component inside PostgreSQL - concern: supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning of an LLM needs a small model to fit 24 GB

title: InferDB: In-Database Machine Learning Inference Using Indexes
note: index-based approximation of end-to-end ML inference pipelines inside PostgreSQL

title: 2DIO: Configurable and Cache-Accurate Trace Generation for Storage Benchmarking
note: Cache-accurate synthetic I/O trace generator with tunable hit-ratio curves - README shows a user-space C++ and Python build with no root requirement. Excellent fit for cache policy work

title: DILI: A Distribution-Driven Learned Index
note: Distribution-driven learned index; C++ single node, SOSD-style datasets

title: Learned Index Benefits: Machine Learning Based Index Performance Estimation
note: ML-based index performance/benefit estimation for index tuning; PostgreSQL plus lightweight models, CPU-only

title: Gem: Scalable Monotonic Graph Processing Beyond Billion-Scale on a Single Machine
note: out-of-core graph engine with pruning for monotonic algorithms on a single machine - I/O-centric user-space engine - concern: largest graph (42B edges) will not fit the 257 GB of free disk

title: Accelerating LLM Serving for Multi-turn Dialogues with Efficient Resource Management
note: KV reuse across dialogue turns plus a length-aware scheduling policy to avoid head-of-line blocking - single-GPU mechanism; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: PathWeaver: A High-Throughput Multi-GPU System for Graph-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Multi-GPU graph-based ANNS; section 5.3 explicitly reports single-GPU gains for ghost staging and the direction-guided techniques, so there is a meaningful single-GPU scale-down. Concern: pipelining-based path extension is inherently multi-GPU and billion-scale datasets exceed 24 GB

title: Groot: Graph-Centric Row Reordering with Tree for Sparse Matrix Multiplications on Tensor Cores
note: Row reordering as a preprocessing pass for SpMM and SDDMM on Tensor Cores; single GPU with standard sparse matrix and GNN datasets. Concern - the repo has no README or description so build effort is unknown, and the kernels are written for SM80 and need an SM86 check

title: PLA-Serve: A Prefill-Length-Aware LLM Serving System
note: Prefill-length-aware dual-queue scheduling and CUDA-Graph-based clustering on SGLang, with a documented artifact including scheduler docs and data. Concern: the multi-instance spatial-disaggregation results need several GPUs; temporal disaggregation on one prefill instance is still reproducible

title: MegaBlocks: Efficient Sparse Training with Mixture-of-Experts
note: Block-sparse GPU kernels for MoE layers - the kernels and the no-token-dropping formulation are single-GPU contributions and the artifact claims a 30 second microbenchmark - concern - paper uses A100 and Docker so it needs a user-space rebuild and the Ampere A5000 has less bandwidth and no A100-class shared memory
